findings.title: Installer-vs-authenticated-user check is skipped when the Integration row does not exist yet
findings.body: The new user-identity check is only reached when an `Integration` row with this `external_id` already exists: the first lookup `Integration.objects.get(external_id=installation_id)` raises `Integration.DoesNotExist` in the normal case where the `installation` webhook has not yet created the Integration, and that branch returns `pipeline.next_step()` immediately (line 481-482). Execution then goes straight to `build_integration`, which builds/creates the Integration from `get_installation_info` without ever comparing `pipeline.fetch_state("github_authenticated_user")` against anything. `build_integration` also only sets `metadata["sender"]` when `state.get("sender")` is truthy, and no view in this pipeline binds a `sender` state. Consequently the PR's stated guarantee — the pipeline fails on a mismatch between the authenticated GitHub user and the user who installed the app — does not hold in the window before the installation webhook is processed (or if that webhook is delayed/lost). Anyone with the `installation_id` who can complete the pipeline during that window can attach the installation, which defeats the cross-tenant protection this PR is meant to add. The path should fail closed when the installer identity cannot be determined.

findings.title: KeyError on integration.metadata["sender"]["login"] yields a 500 instead of the failure page
findings.body: The comparison reads `integration.metadata["sender"]["login"]` directly. `sender` is only present in metadata when the Integration was created by the GitHub `installation` webhook; Integrations created through this pipeline (the `DoesNotExist` branch), Integrations created before `sender` started being recorded, or any Integration whose metadata lacks `sender` will raise `KeyError` here. That turns an expected rejection into an unhandled 500 error page, and it is reachable for example when an Integration exists with no `OrganizationIntegration` (e.g. orphaned/reinstalled integration) and metadata has no `sender`. Use `(integration.metadata.get("sender") or {}).get("login")` and treat a missing login as a failed validation (error page), not an exception.

findings.title: test_installation_not_found no longer exercises the installation 404 path
findings.body: The second request passes `state="ddd023d87a913d5226e2a882c4c4cc05"`, which is not the pipeline signature, so `OAuthLoginView` returns the generic "Invalid installation request." before the pipeline ever reaches `GitHubInstallation`/`build_integration`. The stubbed 404 for `/app/installations/{id}` is therefore never hit, and the previous assertion for "The GitHub installation could not be found." was replaced with the generic message. The test name no longer matches what it verifies and the 404 handling in `build_integration` is now untested. It should use the correct signature and assert the intended installation-not-found error.

findings.title: Token exchange and /user calls are unguarded and can surface as 500 errors
findings.body: `safe_urlopen` at line 423 and `get_user_info(payload["access_token"])` at line 434 are outside any try/except; only the decoding of the token response body is wrapped. A network/connection failure during the access-token exchange, or a non-2xx response from GitHub's `/user` endpoint (invalid/expired token, rate limit, GitHub outage) will raise out of `dispatch`, producing a 500 rather than the intended `error()` failure page that the PR describes for all failure modes. These calls should be wrapped and mapped to the same failure response.
